title: Games
statementMd:
Manao works on a sports TV. He's spent much time watching the football games of some country. After a while he began to notice different patterns. For example, each team has two sets of uniforms: home uniform and guest uniform. When a team plays a game at home, the players put on the home uniform. When a team plays as a guest on somebody else's stadium, the players put on the guest uniform. The only exception to that rule is: when the home uniform color of the host team matches the guests' uniform, the host team puts on its guest uniform as well. For each team the color of the home and guest uniform is different.

There are $*n*$ teams taking part in the national championship. The championship consists of $*n*·(*n* - 1)$ games: each team invites each other team to its stadium. At this point Manao wondered: how many times during the championship is a host team going to put on the guest uniform? Note that the order of the games does not affect this number.

You know the colors of the home and guest uniform for each team. For simplicity, the colors are numbered by integers in such a way that no two distinct colors have the same number. Help Manao find the answer to his question.

## Input

The first line contains an integer $*n*$ ($2 ≤ *n* ≤ 30$). Each of the following $*n*$ lines contains a pair of distinct space-separated integers $*h*_{*i*}$, $*a*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *h*_{*i*}, *a*_{*i*} ≤ 100$) — the colors of the $*i*$-th team's home and guest uniforms, respectively.

## Output

In a single line print the number of games where the host team is going to play in the guest uniform.

## Note

In the first test case the championship consists of 6 games. The only game with the event in question is the game between teams 2 and 1 on the stadium of team 2.

In the second test sample the host team will have to wear guest uniform in the games between teams: 1 and 2, 2 and 1, 2 and 3, 3 and 4, 4 and 2 (the host team is written first).
statementZhMd:
Manao 在一家体育电视台工作。他花了很多时间观看某个国家的足球比赛。过了一段时间后，他开始注意到一些不同的规律。例如，每支球队都有两套队服：主场队服和客场队服。当一支球队在主场进行比赛时，球员会穿主场队服。当一支球队作为客队在其他球队的体育场比赛时，球员会穿客场队服。唯一的例外是：当主队的主场队服颜色与客队的队服颜色相同时，主队也会穿客场队服。对于每支球队来说，主场队服和客场队服的颜色不同。

共有 $*n*$ 支球队参加全国锦标赛。锦标赛由 $*n*·(*n* - 1)$ 场比赛组成：每支球队都邀请其他每支球队到自己的体育场进行比赛。这时 Manao 想知道：在整个锦标赛期间，主队将有多少次穿着客场队服？注意，比赛的顺序不会影响这个数量。

你知道每支球队主场队服和客场队服的颜色。为简单起见，颜色用整数编号，并且任意两个不同的颜色都有不同的编号。请帮助 Manao 找出答案。

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$（$2 ≤ *n* ≤ 30$）。接下来的 $*n*$ 行中，每行包含两个用空格分隔的不同整数 $*h*_{*i*}$、$*a*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *h*_{*i*}, *a*_{*i*} ≤ 100$），分别表示第 $i$ 支球队的主场队服和客场队服的颜色。

## 输出格式

在一行中输出主队将穿着客场队服进行比赛的场次数。

## 说明

在第一个测试用例中，锦标赛由 6 场比赛组成。唯一发生所述情况的比赛是球队 2 与球队 1 的比赛，比赛在球队 2 的体育场进行。

在第二个样例中，主队必须在以下比赛中穿着客场队服：球队 1 和球队 2、球队 2 和球队 1、球队 2 和球队 3、球队 3 和球队 4、球队 4 和球队 2 之间的比赛（主队写在前面）。
